palette.name: MONO.DARK
palette.notes: The parent page requested a dark monochrome treatment. All chart marks use only the Lieflat dark gray ladder; green and all other hues are absent.

template_notes: The catalog calls the barcode L3, while its actual card and render block in lupi-gallery.html are numbered 2. The card title and implementation match, so the chart uses that actual source block and documents the numbering mismatch here.

diagrams.data_shape: Daily commits across approximately 72 calendar days, including zero-commit days.

candidate_comparison.fit: Selected: Lupi's day-by-day sequence makes each calendar date a visible record, and its 90-day scale covers the 72-day history.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: The original uses weekends as a separate mark style; this chart reserves mark placement for the real commit count and includes zero days explicitly.

candidate_comparison.fit: A legitimate daily series for short date ranges.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: The catalog caps it at 30 days, far shorter than this history.

candidate_comparison.fit: A daily sequence can be shown as a continuous activity shape.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: It is intended for 30–60 days and emphasizes the area shape; the 72-day story needs every daily record to remain inspectable.

diagrams.selected_geometry: L3's full-height calendar hairline per day, a value-positioned lollipop dot with stem, three spaced peak labels, and month labels.
diagrams.encoding: One dot and one vertical hairline per date. Dot height is proportional to commits; a zero-commit day stays at the baseline and remains present. Daily author counts appear in the point readout when supplied.
diagrams.interaction: Each date is a real record. Pointer and roving keyboard focus update the caption; click or Enter/Space pins it. No source link is fabricated when the activity record has no URL.

diagrams.data_shape: Top eight commit-attributed identities with exact commit totals.

candidate_comparison.fit: Selected: the catalog is built for horizontal ranked comparisons with up to eight countable rows, so long identities fit better than vertical category labels.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: The source example uses one tick per release; this chart uses a larger declared unit and a proportional final remainder.

candidate_comparison.fit: A ranked unit chart can compare countable categories and can display each contributor as a row of marks.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: Its cascading diagonal and dense point field favor a poster-like ranking; F5 provides a clearer horizontal queue for exact commit totals and names.

candidate_comparison.card_title: Revenue by plan, rung by rung
candidate_comparison.fit: It handles up to eight countable categories with explicit one-unit marks.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: Vertical bars spend width on long login labels and weaken the requested ranking read; F5 has the more suitable horizontal geometry.

diagrams.selected_geometry: F5's aligned horizontal rows, countable vertical ticks, every-fifth-unit marker, and row-end total.
diagrams.encoding: One full tick equals 25 commits; a shorter final tick has length proportional to the remainder divided by 25. Row-end labels retain each exact total. Only real top-eight login records are drawn.
diagrams.interaction: A tick reports its contributor and commit unit; pinning a mark adds the source profile link from the provided contributor record. Login labels are shortened only on the SVG; accessible names and readouts retain the complete login.

diagrams.data_shape: 315 distinct merged-PR authors grouped by exactly one merged PR versus multiple merged PRs.

candidate_comparison.card_title: A hundred of us, four minds
candidate_comparison.fit: Selected: its unit-decomposition contract lets every dot stand for one actual person; the two author groups remain directly countable and sum to the 315 supplied identities.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: The source example uses 100 respondents. This adapts the same phyllotaxis field to the actual 315 identities and uses area-scaled cluster spread, without inventing respondents.

candidate_comparison.fit: Can show countable units across ranked categories.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: Its cascade ranks category totals and separates categories along a diagonal; it makes individual account inspection and the two-way composition less direct.

candidate_comparison.fit: Two categories fit its small composition limit.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: A donut would aggregate the 315 accounts into shares and discard the requested one-dot-per-author identity.

diagrams.selected_geometry: L14's two point fields use deterministic golden-angle placement, countable dots, every-fifth-point spokes, and grouped labels.
diagrams.encoding: Each dot comes from one real mergedAuthors record. The lightest ladder value denotes repeat authors; a lower-contrast gray denotes authors with exactly one merged PR. Cluster membership and dot count encode category and number of people, not star counts.
diagrams.interaction: All 315 records are inspectable through one roving tab stop per SVG. Focus or hover identifies the login and merged-PR total; click or Enter/Space pins the real profile URL from the record.

diagrams.data_shape: Frequency across six supplied merge-duration bins for 80 merged PRs in a bounded, recent-closed-PR sample.

candidate_comparison.card_title: Revenue by plan, rung by rung
candidate_comparison.fit: Selected: six supplied bins fall within its eight-category limit, and each count is a small exact integer that can be drawn as countable PR rungs.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: The title and bin labels are adapted to merge durations; no interpolation is made between duration buckets.

candidate_comparison.fit: Could compare six bins with exact horizontal unit marks.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: Its queue shape emphasizes a ranking; the vertical rung form more clearly preserves the supplied frequency-by-bin structure.

candidate_comparison.card_title: Most tickets resolve within six hours
candidate_comparison.fit: Its domain is single-variable binned frequency, and the merge-duration bins have explicit time boundaries.
candidate_comparison.tradeoff: F14 is the fallback histogram template. F1 already carries these six categories with exact one-PR rungs, so the mainline template can encode the data without adding a second shape or implying a continuous bar.

diagrams.selected_geometry: F1's independent countable rung stacks, shared baseline, peak count labels, and category labels.
diagrams.encoding: One rung equals one merged PR in that duration bin. Bin counts come from the matching real records; the chart does not draw a continuous bar or infer durations between bin boundaries.
diagrams.interaction: Every rung is linked to a sampled PR record and reports its exact sampled duration; clicking or pressing Enter/Space pins the PR URL. The readout keeps the bounded sample definition visible.

accessibility.svg: Every chart SVG has a title, description, role=group, and a description link to its readout.
accessibility.keyboard: One data mark per chart is in the tab order. Arrow keys move between marks; Home and End jump to the first and last mark; Enter/Space pins; Escape clears a pin.
accessibility.pointer: Hover updates the human-readable readout and the page-level #chart-tooltip element; click pins the current record and its GitHub source link where available.
accessibility.motion: Lieflat-style reveal runs when each SVG enters view; clicking the empty SVG restarts it. prefers-reduced-motion disables animation.
accessibility.tables: Accessible expandable data tables are provided by the parent page, outside this module.
